tasks.short: Work out where we stand financially now and in three to twelve months: cash, margin, covenants.

today.trigger: Month close, a board meeting, a bank covenant date, or a big customer win or loss
steps: Pull trial balance and debtor/creditor ageing from AFAS Profit into Excel
Ask the FP&A Analysts for the latest forecast and flex worker cost run-rate
Rebuild the cash and covenant headroom view by hand
Check margin per site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) against budget
Write a short view for the management team
drudgery: Re-keying AFAS exports into the same Excel model every month
Matching agency invoices to hours to get the real flex cost
today.time_sinks: Collecting and reconciling numbers takes most of the time; the thinking is the last hour.

lenses.faster: A nightly pipeline from AFAS and Rabobank keeps a 13-week cash and covenant view current, so the manual rebuild disappears.
lenses.autonomous: The model reruns after the nightly AFAS refresh and alerts the Finance Director when cash headroom or a covenant ratio crosses a set threshold.
lenses.ambitious: A rolling 18-month view per site and per large customer, refreshed weekly instead of a quarterly snapshot.
lenses.joy: No more copying exports; the Finance Director spends the time on what the numbers mean for the business.
lenses.options: Every update comes with base, downside (lost customer, peak season with less flex labour) and upside scenarios side by side.
lenses.altitude: The Finance Director owns the model's assumptions and thresholds and checks its accuracy each month instead of building it.

tasks.human_edge: Judging which risks are real, knowing what customers and the bank will do, and owning the message to the board.
tasks.pattern_why: Several sources and steps with exceptions (missing invoices, one-off items); the Finance Director must approve the view before it goes to the board or bank.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract refresh and month close
steps: Load AFAS ledger, ageing and Rabobank balances into the model
Update the 13-week cash and covenant ratios on fixed rules
LLM drafts a commentary on movements and scenario results
Flag thresholds breached and items it could not explain
Finance Director reviews, edits and releases
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director approves every version shared outside Finance.
data_needed: General ledger and budget per site
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint Finance site, versioned forecast file with commentary history

evidence.claim: Power BI can run on a nightly AFAS extract and show cash and margin dashboards
evidence.source: Power BI; company already uses it on AFAS extract

evidence.claim: Copilot in Excel can draft commentary and scenario tables from a workbook
An agent reliably explains month-on-month movements for a mid-size logistics firm

risks: Commentary sounds confident about movements it misread
Forecast quality limited by late agency invoices
Over-trust in thresholds set once and never reviewed
research_questions: How many hours a month go into rebuilding the cash and covenant view today?
Does the AFAS extract include everything needed (accruals, agency hours) or are manual adjustments always required?
How accurate was last year's forecast, and which errors would earlier data have caught?

tasks.short: Check credit applications from new customers and our own financing requests (truck leases, bank facility).

today.trigger: Sales signs a new shipper, a customer asks for a higher credit limit, or a lease or facility renewal comes up
steps: Get a credit report and KvK extract on the customer
Check payment history in AFAS if it is an existing customer
Agree a limit and payment terms with Sales and the Credit and Collections Officer
For own financing, compare lease and loan offers and prepare figures for Rabobank
drudgery: Copying data from credit reports and annual accounts into a template
Chasing Sales for missing customer details
today.time_sinks: Waiting on information and filling templates, not deciding.

lenses.faster: An agent assembles the credit file (credit score, KvK data, filed accounts, AFAS payment behaviour) and proposes a limit in minutes.
lenses.autonomous: A new debtor record in AFAS or a limit breach triggers the check; small limits inside policy are set automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Every customer's limit is reviewed quarterly against payment behaviour, not only at onboarding.
lenses.joy: No more template filling; the Finance Director only looks at the large and unusual cases.
lenses.options: For financing, the agent lays out lease versus loan versus facility draw with cost and covenant effects.
lenses.altitude: The Finance Director writes the credit policy and limit rules and audits how the system applies them.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer onboarding checks

tasks.human_edge: Relationship with key customers and the bank, and taking the risk call on large or strategic accounts.
tasks.pattern_why: Gathers from several sources and handles exceptions; a person must approve limits above policy and any financing decision.

in_practice.trigger: New debtor created in AFAS or limit increase request from Sales
steps: Pull credit report, KvK data and AFAS payment history
Score against the written credit policy
Draft a credit memo with proposed limit and terms
Auto-approve within policy limits; route others to the Finance Director
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director approves limits above the policy threshold and all financing proposals.
data_needed: Customer KvK number and filed accounts
in_practice.logs_to: Credit memo in SharePoint linked to the AFAS debtor record

evidence.claim: Creditsafe provides credit scores and limits for Dutch companies via API
An LLM can draft a credit memo from structured credit data

risks: Automated limits that are too generous for thin-file new businesses
Credit decisions about sole traders touch personal data under AVG/GDPR
Sales pressure to override the policy
research_questions: How many credit decisions a month are routine versus above policy?
What were bad-debt losses last three years, and would a rules-based check have flagged them?
Does the credit agency data cover the small transport subcontractors and shippers Noordhaven serves?

tasks.short: Go through the debtor ageing and collection status to see what is overdue and why.

today.trigger: Weekly cash meeting and month close
steps: Export debtor ageing from AFAS
Read the Credit and Collections Officer's notes on disputes and promises
Discuss top overdue accounts with the officer and Sales
Decide on escalation or credit stop
drudgery: Re-sorting the same ageing list every week
Reading through email threads to find why an invoice is unpaid
today.time_sinks: Finding the reason behind each overdue invoice.

lenses.faster: A Power BI page shows ageing, DSO trend and top movers, with dispute reasons pulled from notes and mail, so the review takes minutes.
lenses.autonomous: Alerts fire when a key account passes 60 days or a promise to pay is missed; the dashboard updates nightly without anyone asking.
lenses.ambitious: DSO tracked per customer, per site and per invoice type, with root causes (missing POD, rate disputes) fed back to operations.
lenses.joy: No list sorting; only the accounts that need a decision reach the Finance Director.
lenses.options: For each problem account, suggested actions: reminder, call, credit stop, or settlement offer, with cash effect.
lenses.altitude: The Finance Director sets escalation rules and DSO targets and checks whether the process is working.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer weekly reporting

tasks.human_edge: Deciding when to stop service to a big customer and handling the commercial conversation.
tasks.pattern_why: Ageing and DSO are rule-based on structured AFAS data; a small LLM step only classifies dispute reasons from notes.

steps: Compute ageing, DSO and movement per customer
LLM classifies dispute reasons from collection notes and emails
Flag accounts that break escalation rules
Weekly summary sent to the Finance Director in Teams
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director decides on credit stops and write-offs.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI dataset history and AFAS debtor notes

evidence.claim: Power BI dashboards on AFAS debtor data are common in Dutch mid-size firms
LLMs classify free-text dispute notes into reason codes accurately

risks: Dispute notes are incomplete, so reasons get misclassified
Dashboard hides context a conversation would give
research_questions: How consistently does the Credit and Collections Officer log notes in AFAS?
What share of overdue value comes from the top 20 customers?
Which dispute reasons recur, and do operations fix them?

tasks.short: Prepare the board pack, annual accounts, bank covenant reports and statutory filings.

today.trigger: Monthly board meeting, quarterly covenant report, year-end audit, CBS and tax deadlines
steps: Pull figures from AFAS and reconcile with the Controller
Fill the board pack and covenant templates in Excel and PowerPoint
Draft the notes to the annual accounts and management report
Answer auditor questions
Sign off and file
drudgery: Copying the same numbers into several templates
Updating last year's text in notes and reports
today.time_sinks: Reconciling figures between versions and rewriting standard text.

lenses.faster: Templates fill from one approved data set, and an LLM drafts notes and commentary from the prior year and the movements.
lenses.autonomous: After close is locked, the covenant report and board pack draft are generated automatically and placed for review.
lenses.ambitious: Board gets a monthly pack with site-level KPIs and clear commentary, and sustainability data is prepared properly if CSRD scope applies after the EU Omnibus changes.
lenses.joy: No copy-paste between files; the Finance Director edits the story instead of the tables.
lenses.options: Two or three drafts of the board narrative with different emphasis to choose from.
lenses.altitude: The Finance Director owns the reporting data model and the review checklist rather than assembling packs.

tasks.human_edge: Signing, judgement on estimates and disclosures, and answering the board, auditor and bank.
tasks.pattern_why: Multi-step with fixed templates and legal liability; every report must be approved before filing.

steps: Generate tables from the locked AFAS data set
Run reconciliation checks between ledger and reports
LLM drafts commentary and notes with tracked changes
Controller reviews numbers, Finance Director reviews text and signs
in_practice.human_gate: Controller and Finance Director approve; auditor reviews statutory accounts.
data_needed: Covenant definitions from the Rabobank agreement
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint versioned reporting folder with approval record

evidence.claim: Copilot in Word and PowerPoint can draft text and slides from source documents
Auditors accept AI-drafted notes when the company reviews and owns them

risks: Errors in filed reports carry legal and covenant consequences
Drafted text copies last year's wording that no longer fits
Auditor may require more documentation of the process
research_questions: How many hours go into the board pack and covenant reports each month?
Which numbers are re-keyed rather than linked today?
What does the external auditor require when AI tools draft parts of the annual report?

tasks.short: Look at how finance processes and systems work and propose changes to controls, procedures and budgets.

today.trigger: Audit findings, rising close time, a new system request, or annual planning
steps: Collect complaints and audit management letter points
Ask the team how invoices, close and collections actually run
Analyse volumes and touch rates in AFAS
Write a proposal and discuss with management and the Controller
drudgery: Gathering process data by asking people
Writing up the current process from scratch
today.time_sinks: Understanding how the process really runs before you can improve it.

lenses.faster: Analysis of AFAS workflow logs shows touchless invoice rates, approval delays and close task durations without interviews.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly control dashboard shows exceptions (late approvals, segregation-of-duties breaks) as they happen.
lenses.ambitious: Continuous improvement of procure to pay and close with a clear target such as close in five working days.
lenses.joy: Less detective work, more designing the better process with the team.
lenses.options: Several redesign options with expected hours saved, cost and risk for each.
lenses.altitude: The Finance Director becomes the designer of the finance operating model and its controls.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst AFAS configuration advice

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what to change, getting the team and the works council on board where roles change, and owning control design.
tasks.pattern_why: The work is judgement and change; AI speeds up analysis and drafting but the Finance Director leads.

in_practice.trigger: Quarterly process review or audit finding
steps: Pull workflow and timestamp data from AFAS
AI summarises bottlenecks and exceptions
AI drafts improvement options with estimates
Finance Director chooses and presents
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director decides; works council consulted if jobs or monitoring change (WOR article 27).

evidence.claim: Process mining tools analyse ERP event logs to find bottlenecks
AFAS workflow logs are detailed enough for this analysis

risks: Monitoring individual employees' task times needs works council consent
Data shows what happens, not why
research_questions: Can AFAS workflow timestamps be exported at invoice level?
What share of supplier invoices is processed without touch today?
Which audit findings repeated in the last two years?

tasks.short: Make the monthly operational and risk reports for the management team.

steps: Collect cost per site, flex labour use, absence costs and margin
Update the risk register (customer concentration, fuel, labour shortage)
Build charts in Excel and PowerPoint
Write commentary
drudgery: Rebuilding the same charts every month
Combining agency data from three portals
today.time_sinks: Collecting data from different sources and formatting it.

lenses.faster: Fixed Power BI report with an LLM-drafted commentary; the Finance Director only edits.
lenses.autonomous: The report is ready the morning after close, with risks scored on agreed indicators.
lenses.ambitious: Weekly site-level reports for site managers, not just a monthly management team pack.
lenses.joy: No chart building; time goes to discussing the risks with the managers.
lenses.options: Commentary drafts at different lengths for the management team and for site managers.
lenses.altitude: The Finance Director defines indicators and risk thresholds and reviews whether they predict problems.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which risk matters this month and saying it plainly to colleagues.
tasks.pattern_why: Data and charts are deterministic; the LLM turns movements into a draft commentary inside a fixed workflow.

steps: Refresh Power BI report from AFAS and agency data
Score risk indicators against thresholds
LLM drafts commentary and risk changes
Finance Director edits and sends
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director reviews commentary before distribution.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI can generate narrative summaries of report pages
Agency portal data can be extracted automatically

risks: Agency portals may not offer exports or APIs
Absence data in reports must be aggregated to respect AVG/GDPR
research_questions: Do the three staffing agencies provide hours and invoice data in a machine-readable format?
Which charts in the pack does the management team actually use?
How long does the pack take today from close to distribution?

tasks.short: Analyse cost data to set next year's budget per site and department.

today.trigger: Annual budget cycle (autumn) and mid-year reforecast
steps: Export actual costs per site from AFAS
Add CAO wage increases, headcount plans and flex labour needs
Collect input from site managers in Excel
Consolidate, challenge and iterate
Present to management and inform the works council
drudgery: Chasing and merging Excel files from site managers
Recalculating wage costs after each CAO change
today.time_sinks: Collecting inputs and redoing the consolidation after every change.

lenses.faster: A driver-based model calculates wage cost from AFAS headcount and CAO tables, flex cost from volume, and diesel from usage, so the base budget is ready in days.
lenses.autonomous: The model updates when a CAO increase or headcount change is recorded in AFAS.
lenses.ambitious: Budgets per customer contract and per site, with rolling reforecasts each quarter.
lenses.joy: No merging files; time goes into challenging the plans with site managers.
lenses.options: Budget scenarios for volume up or down, CAO outcome and flex share.
lenses.altitude: The Finance Director owns the drivers and assumptions; FP&A runs the model.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist wage cost projections

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating targets with site managers and the management team, and explaining the budget to the works council.
tasks.pattern_why: Calculation is deterministic but the budget is a negotiated decision led by the Finance Director.

steps: Load actuals and headcount from AFAS
Apply CAO tables and volume drivers
AI drafts variance explanations and scenarios
Site managers adjust in a shared form
Finance Director challenges and approves
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director and management team approve the budget; works council informed (WOR article 31a).
in_practice.logs_to: Budget versions in SharePoint with change log

evidence.claim: Copilot in Excel can build and explain scenario tables
Driver-based budgeting reduces budget cycle time

risks: Wrong driver assumptions spread through the whole budget
Individual salary data must stay restricted
research_questions: How many weeks does the budget cycle take today?
Are customer volumes reliable enough to drive cost budgets?
Can CAO wage tables be held as structured data linked to AFAS?

tasks.short: Follow diesel, energy, interest and price index movements that affect our costs and customer rates.

today.trigger: Monthly cost review, customer contract indexation dates, facility interest resets
steps: Look up diesel prices, Euribor, CBS price indices and energy prices
Compare with what is in customer contracts and budgets
Calculate the effect on margin
Advise Sales on surcharges or indexation
drudgery: Manually looking up the same indices each month
Checking which contracts have which indexation clause
today.time_sinks: Finding the right index and contract clause for each customer.

lenses.faster: Indices are pulled automatically and applied to a contract table, so the margin effect is ready without lookups.
lenses.autonomous: Indexation letters are drafted when a contract's index date arrives; a fuel surcharge is calculated when diesel moves past a threshold.
lenses.ambitious: Every customer contract gets correct, on-time indexation, which today some probably miss.
lenses.joy: No lookups; the Finance Director focuses on pricing advice to Sales.
lenses.options: Surcharge and indexation options with the margin and customer risk for each.
lenses.altitude: The Finance Director maintains the index rules and the contract clause register.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding when to push a price increase onto a key customer and how hard.
tasks.pattern_why: Index data is structured and clauses can be written as rules; an LLM step extracts clauses from contracts once.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly index publication and contract index dates
steps: Fetch diesel, CBS CPI and Euribor data
LLM extracts indexation clauses from SharePoint contracts into a table, checked once by a person
Calculate cost and margin effect per contract
Draft indexation letters and alerts
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director and Sales approve any price change before it goes to the customer.

evidence.claim: CBS publishes price indices through an open data API
LLMs extract indexation clauses from contracts reliably enough with human checking

risks: Misread clauses lead to wrong invoices and customer disputes
Contracts not all stored in SharePoint
research_questions: How many customer contracts have indexation or fuel clauses, and were all applied last year?
What is the margin effect of a 10% diesel move?
Are all signed contracts available as searchable files?

role.altitude: From building numbers to owning the finance system: the data model, assumptions, thresholds and controls that produce forecasts, reports and credit decisions, checked monthly for accuracy.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer credit checks and escalation
Sales pricing and contract indexation support
HR Director workforce and absence cost reporting
role.ceiling_note: About 300 to 350 of the roughly 685 hours in these tasks could be freed. The ceiling is set by signatures and liability (annual accounts, covenants), negotiation with the bank, customers and site managers, works council consultation, and data quality from AFAS and the three agency portals.
skills_to_grow: Designing and testing controls for AI-assisted workflows
Data model ownership on AFAS and Power BI
Clear writing for the board and management
AVG/GDPR and EU AI Act basics for finance data use
role.ambitious_version: Close the month in five working days with a rolling 18-month forecast per site and customer that the management team uses for decisions, and correct indexation on every contract, run by a finance team that spends its time on analysis and advice.
